name: Qwen Image 2.1 — reshoot from another angle (multiple angles)
description:
Reshoot the same subject from a different camera position. Upload one photo, pick an angle and a height, and Qwen-Image-2.1 with a camera-control adapter renders that subject as seen from there — the back of an object really is its back, not a mirrored front.

WHAT IT IS FOR, AND WHERE IT BREAKS — measured on this rig, one seed, back view, at the settings this card ships with:
• ✓ BEST — a single subject on a plain or simple background: a rendered character, a product, a studio portrait. The camera genuinely goes round it and the subject keeps its identity, clothing and colours. This is what it was trained on (Objaverse turntable renders).
• ✓ GOOD — a real photo of one person against a backdrop. Tested on a full-figure press photo: it came back from behind with the jacket, trousers and shoes intact.
• ⚠ PARTIAL — a subject inside a busy scene. The SUBJECT turns correctly, but the BACKGROUND is re-invented rather than re-photographed from the new angle: a workshop of pipes and gears came back as a different workshop. Use it when the subject is what matters and the setting is not.
• ✗ NOT FOR THIS — a scene with no single subject: architecture, interiors, landscapes. Asked for the back of a castle, the camera does not move at all and you get a re-rendered variant of the same view with details changed. It orbits a SUBJECT; it cannot walk around a place.
• ✗ TEXT AND LOGOS come back as nonsense anywhere in the frame — a turn is a re-render, not a rotation of your pixels.

★ The prompt is BUILT FOR YOU from the two dropdowns. The adapter answers only to its own grammar, which starts with the trigger word <mva>, and a prompt missing it produces a perfectly plausible picture with the camera never having moved — so the trigger is wired into the graph as a fixed literal instead of being something to remember. 12 angles × 8 heights (each with a close-up variant) = 96 framings, and every one is the documented spelling.

★ To build a turnaround, schedule it once per angle on the same photo and the same seed — the dropdown is in turning order, so working down it walks the camera around the subject.

★ 'Adapter version' switches between the author's two releases on the same picture and seed. The author recommends **v2**, but **v1 is the default here** and the reason is this rig: v1 was trained on a *convrot8 int8* base, which is the Qwen-Image-2.1 build installed on this machine, while v2 was trained on *bf16 full precision*. Compared on one photo and seed, v1 comes back more photographic and v2 slightly more CGI-like. Try v2 — it is one field — and on a rig running the bf16 base it may well win. Strength 0.8–1.0 — start at 1.0, and if the result drifts back toward simply copying your photo, lower it to 0.8 rather than switching version.

⚠⚠ Keep 'Reference size' at 1 MP. The adapter was TRAINED on 512×512 renders, and this bundle originally scaled your photo to match — that was a mistake, measured and corrected: at 512² the reference carries too little for the model to hold on to and the result collapses into the flat, plain-background look of its Objaverse training renders. At 1 MP on the same photo and seed it stays photographic — film grain, an earring, a jacket weave correctly continued round the back. Training size and reference size are not the same thing.

⚠ A turn is a re-render, so anything the original photo could not see is invented, and fine detail like fur or fabric weave softens. Judge the result against the subject, not the pixels.

Licence: the adapter is Apache 2.0, unusually permissive for this family — but the Qwen-Image-2.1 base it runs on is Qwen Research, research and evaluation only, so the combination is not for commercial work.

promptGuides.tip: There is nothing to write: the two dropdowns are the whole prompt grammar, and the <mva> trigger is built into the graph. It orbits a SUBJECT — a person, a character, an object — not a place; see the description for what was measured to work and what was not.

models.note: Camera-control LoRA, v2 step 1500, rank 64, trained on Qwen-Image-2.1 at 512². Trigger '<mva>'. Renamed on download from the repo's 80-character checkpoint filename. 192 of 192 modules map onto this rig's fused int8-convrot build.
The v1 release, step 1000, rank 32. Kept so the two can be compared on one picture and seed; the author recommends v2.

exposedParameters.label: The subject to reshoot — one clear photo, the subject filling the frame
Camera angle — where the camera stands, going round the subject
Camera height and framing — eye level, raised, high, or straight down
Adapter version (v1 is the better match for this rig’s base build)
Adapter strength (0.8–1.0; lower it if the camera will not move)
Reference size in megapixels — how much of your photo the model gets to see, and the size of the result. Lower loses detail fast.
Steps (40 is the author’s own setting)
Seed — keep it fixed across angles to build a consistent turnaround
